Henrard in South India.]] '''''Bothriochloa''''' is a common and widespread [[genus]] of plants in the [[Poaceae|grass family]] native to many countries on all inhabited continents and many islands.{{cite web|url= http://delta-intkey.com/grass/www/bothrioc.htm |title=The grass genera of the world: descriptions, illustrations, identification, and information retrieval; including synonyms, morphology, anatomy, physiology, phytochemistry, cytology, classification, pathogens, world and local distribution, and references |access-date=2009-08-19 |author=Watson L, Dallwitz MJ. |year=2008 |work=The Grass Genera of the World }} They are often called '''beardgrass''', '''bluegrass''' or '''bluestem'''. Some species are invasive in areas where they have been introduced.[http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?8738,8841 Jepson Manual Treatment][https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=BOTHR United States Department of Agriculture Plants Profile] The [[etymology]] of the genus name ''Bothriochloa'' derives from the two [[ancient Greek]] words {{wikt-lang|grc|βοθρίον}} ({{grc-transl|βοθρίον}}), meaning "small pit or trench", and {{wikt-lang|grc|χλόη}} or {{wikt-lang|grc|χλόα}} ({{grc-transl|χλόα}}), meaning "new green shoot or blade of grass".{{Cite book |title=Abrégé du dictionnaire grec français |last=Bailly |first=Anatole |date=1981-01-01 |publisher=Hachette |isbn=978-2010035289 |location=Paris |oclc=461974285 }}{{Cite web |url=http://www.tabularium.be/bailly/ |title=Greek-french dictionary online |last=Bailly |first=Anatole |date= |website=www.tabularium.be |publisher= |access-date=October 8, 2020}}{{Cite web |url=http://jan.ucc.nau.edu/~plants-c/bio414/species%20pages/Bothriochloa%20barbinodis.htm |title=Ellen Dorn, Native Plants of Arizona 2004, ''Bothriochloa barbinodis'' (Lag.) Herter |access-date=2011-12-23 |archive-date=2015-04-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402090215/http://jan.ucc.nau.edu/~plants-c/bio414/species%20pages/Bothriochloa%20barbinodis.htm |url-status=dead }} Recently, some specimens of ''Bothriochloa'' were collected from Gooty Fort Hill, Andhra Pradesh, India and identified as ''Bothriochloa ewartiana'' (Domin) C. E. Hubb. based on literature study and international correspondence with experts from Australia, Indonesia and Americas.{{Cite journal |last1=Landge |first1=Shahid Nawaz |last2=Shinde |first2=Rajendra D. |date=20 August 2021 |title=Synopsis of the genus ''Bothriochloa'' (Poaceae: Andropogoneae) in India |url=https://www.biotaxa.org/Phytotaxa/article/view/phytotaxa.516.1.3 |journal=Phytotaxa |volume=516 |issue=1 |pages=43–58 |doi=10.11646/phytotaxa.516.1.3 |s2cid=238722563 |via=Magnolia Press|url-access=subscription }} It formed an extended and disjunct distribution of a Far Eastern species in Asia from India. == Systematics == [[File:Bothriochloa pseudoischaemum (Nees ex Steud.)
